properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued November 11 at 10:48PM PST until November 13 at 6:00PM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the first Coastal Flood Advisory, Up to 1.5 ft of
inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Beach Hazards
Statement, An increased risk for sneaker waves and strong rip
currents with breaking waves of 15 to 20 ft expected. For the
High Surf Warning, Dangerously large breaking waves of 25 to 35
ft, with occasional sets of 40 to 50 ft at favored breakpoints.
For the second Coastal Flood Advisory, large breaking waves will
run up beaches and crash over seawalls, inundating adjacent,
low-lying infrastructure.

* WHERE...San Francisco and Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur
Coast.

* WHEN...For the first Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 PM PST
Friday. For the Beach Hazards Statement, through Friday
afternoon. For the High Surf Warning, from 6 PM Friday to 4 AM
PST Sunday. For the second Coastal Flood Advisory, from
midnight Friday night to 6 PM PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. Dangerously large breaking waves can overpower
swimmers, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties,
and rocks resulting in significant physical injury and
increasing the risk of drowning. Waves can sweep across the
shoreline without warning, pulling people into the sea from
beaches, jetties, and rocks.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tide gauge, high tide
is expected to be: 1.3 ft above normal (7.1 ft MLLW) at 12:10 PM
Thursday 11/12, 1.5 ft above normal (7.3 ft MLLW) at 12:49 PM
Friday 11/13. These predictions include up to 1.8 ft of surge
that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat.
High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the
Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.
The Coastal Flood Advisory on Saturday is specifically for the
Pacific Coast, where large breaking waves will spill over sea
walls and run up beaches onto adjacent infrastructure.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Everyone should remain out of the water due to life-threatening
surf conditions. Stay off of jetties, piers, and other waterside
infrastructure.

Stay off of jetties, piers, rocks, and other waterside
infrastructure. Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous surf
and NEVER turn your back on the ocean. Monitor local weather,
surf and tide forecasts at www.weather.gov/mtr.

properties.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued November 12 at 1:32AM EST until November 13 at 12:00PM EST by NWS Marquette MI
properties.description:
...ACCUMULATING LAKE EFFECT SNOW TONIGHT THROUGH FRIDAY...

.Lake effect snow showers will continue through Friday. Wet snow
accumulations are expected away from the Lake Superior shoreline with
several inches of snowfall over the higher terrain.

* WHAT...Lake effect snow expected. Additional snow accumulations
between 3 and 8 inches over the higher elevations of Marquette and
Baraga Counties with up to 10 inches in rural areas north of US-41
and west of Marquette County Road 510. Less than an inch of snow is
expected near Lake Superior. Winds gusting as high as 25 mph and up
to 35 mph near Lake Superior.

* WHERE...Baraga and Marquette Counties.

* WHEN...Until noon EST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. The hazardous conditions
will impact the Thursday morning and evening commutes along with
the Friday morning commute.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Warmer temperatures near Lake Superior will
limit snow accumulations to less than an inch near the lakeshore,
including the city of Marquette. Conditions will deteriorate as you
move inland, particularly US-41 between Marquette and Negaunee.
Snow accumulations of up to 2" are expected through the rest of the
night, snow showers are expected to increase in intensity this
afternoon into Thursday night.
properties.instruction:
Slow down and use caution while traveling.

During lake effect snow, the weather can vary from bands of locally
heavy snow to dry weather just a few miles away. Visibilities can
also vary greatly. Be prepared for rapid changes in weather,
visibility, and road conditions.
